newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico seeks to subsidise 2 mln T of Sinaloa corn.
newsitem.headline: Mexico seeks to subsidise 2 mln T of Sinaloa corn.

text.p: Mexican farm authorities are working out mechanisms to subsidise the sales of two million tonnes of corn in the northwestern state of Sinaloa, the Agriculture Ministry said Tuesday.

In a statement, the ministry said "a system of stimuli incorporating the transportation and storage of corn" is under study between Conasupo, the national staples agency; Aserca, the national farming support agency; and the Sinaloa state government and the national farm development bank Banrural.
Throughout Mexico, farmers and grains traders have been at loggerheads over domestic prices because of falling international prices.

In recent weeks, the government has stepped in and started to fix grains prices on a state-by-state, product-by-product basis to avoid price wars between farmers and merchandisers, also offering generous farmer subsidies.
In Sinaloa, the ministry already announced an accord on wheat prices and also an expected agreement next week on sorghum prices.
The ministry did not say if corn prices would also be fixed in the state. Sinaloa corn output this year is expected to reach 2.5 million tonnes, part for domestic consumption.

Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida Ochoa said in the statement that Sinaloa farmers would receive a total of 1.56 billion pesos in federal and state subsidies this year, including 650 million pesos for corn production. No information was given for earmarked subsidies for corn sales.
